The aim of this experiment is to determine the internal volume of a test-tube using two
displacement methods.
Carry out the following instructions referring to Figs. 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3. You are supplied with a
beaker of water.

cylinder

parts.label: i
parts.text:
Pour approximately 80 cm3 of water from the beaker into the measuring cylinder.
Record the volume V1 of water.
V 1 =  ......................................................

content.text: Pour approximately 80 cm3 of water from the beaker into the measuring cylinder.
Record the volume V1 of water.

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
Lower the test-tube, closed end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and
push it down until it is filled with water, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Record the new water
level V2.
V2 =  ......................................................

content.html: Lower the test-tube, closed end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and push it down until it is filled with water, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Record the new water level V2.
content.text: Lower the test-tube, closed end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and push it down until it is filled with water, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Record the new water level V2.

parts.label: iii
parts.text:
Calculate the volume VG of the glass of the test-tube using the equation
VG = (V2 – V1).
VG =  ......................................................
[3]

content.html: Calculate the volume VG of the glass of the test-tube using the equation VG = (V2 – V1).
content.text: Calculate the volume VG of the glass of the test-tube using the equation VG = (V2 – V1).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Remove the test-tube from the measuring cylinder and pour the water from the tube and
the measuring cylinder into the beaker.

parts.label: i
parts.text:
Pour approximately 70 cm3 of water from the beaker into the measuring cylinder.
Record the volume V3 of water.
V3 =  ......................................................

content.html: Pour approximately 70 cm3 of water from the beaker into the measuring cylinder. Record the volume V3 of water.
content.text: Pour approximately 70 cm3 of water from the beaker into the measuring cylinder. Record the volume V3 of water.

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
Gently put the test-tube, open end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder
and carefully push it down with your finger or pencil until it is just covered with
water, as shown in Fig. 1.3. Record the new water level V4.
V4 =  ......................................................

content.html: Gently put the test-tube, open end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and carefully push it down with your finger or pencil until it is just covered with water, as shown in Fig. 1.3. Record the new water level V4.
content.text: Gently put the test-tube, open end first, into the water in the measuring cylinder and carefully push it down with your finger or pencil until it is just covered with water, as shown in Fig. 1.3. Record the new water level V4.

content.html: Calculate the increase in water level (V4 – V3).
content.text: Calculate the increase in water level (V4 – V3).

parts.label: iv
parts.text:
Calculate the volume VA of air in the test-tube using the equation VA = (V4 – V3) – VG.
VA =  ......................................................
[3]

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Remove the test-tube from the measuring cylinder and pour the water from the measuring
cylinder into the beaker. Fill the test-tube to the top with water from the beaker. Pour the
water from the test-tube into the measuring cylinder. Record the volume VW of water
from the tube.
VW =  ......................................................
[1]

content.html: Remove the test-tube from the measuring cylinder and pour the water from the measuring cylinder into the beaker. Fill the test-tube to the top with water from the beaker. Pour the water from the test-tube into the measuring cylinder. Record the volume VW of water from the tube.

content.html: The aim of this experiment is to determine the internal volume of the test-tube by two methods. The two values are VA (obtained from parts (a) and (b)) and VW (obtained from part (c)). The values obtained from your readings may not be the same.
